/v/fatpeoplehate verified member here, here's the skinny (lol). I think I remember the chain of events.

Imgur started censoring FPH's images (by removing them, along with some porn images) about the same time that reddit removed us from the frontpage because we looked bad to advertisers. It was around the time we broke 150,000 subscribers.

Knowing the way the wind was blowing, FPH mods warned everyone to behave at this point. There were no brigades.

Shortly after that, slimgur and anotherpage (now picgur) were created as an imgur replacement. FPH users were encouraged to use them instead, since imgur was no longer reliable.

Next, Reddit admins quietly banned slimgur. any post linking a slimgur image was automatically removed. It looked obvious to us that there were some people in the imgur/reddit alliance who had a hate-on for us, and that they were watching us closely.

One of the FPH members went on imgur's site and grabbed the publicly available headshots of their staff (and their dog). He put them together in a single image with the caption "IMGUR STAFF: Even their dog is fat." It was true, too; it's a pretty pudgy dog, and some of them are clearly overweight.

Note: these were images that they made available. There were no names on the FPH image. Imgur has since removed the headshots, of course.

Anyway, this is what is widely believed to be the straw that broke the SJW's back. The day after it was posted Reddit banned FPH. FPH had long ago set up contingency plans for this and was already on voat. Today we have over 15,000 subscribers and growing. And every last one of those people strongly feels that imgur contributed to reddit's attempt to destroy our community.

That is why imgur is just as bad. Because they don't believe in freedom of speech, no matter what their humble beginnings. They believe in censorship.

Also their dog is fat, and that's just animal abuse.

i don't, but if you ask in /v/fatpeoplehate, better scholars than i will likely provide you with screenshots and timestamps. they're good that way. there was a link to an archive of the entire FPH page before its deletion, too.

They purportedly had a lot to do with the original exodus. Essentially fph posted a picture making fun of much of imgur's staff for being overweight, including their dog in retaliation for them believing imgur was taking down a lot of the pics they were making fun of. It was really pretty tame as making fun of people on the internet goes.

The next day fph got banned by reddit to "keep people safe". I don't think anyone believes that is a coincidence, whether they pressured reddit to get rid of it or not is immaterial though, a ton of people think they did. Given that NSFL reddits like picsofdeadkids still exist, most people found their rationale to be lacking. It isn't very difficult to find many communities on reddit that do the same, or worse to people than fph. This led a lot of people to question exactly why it was banned over any of the worse ones, and why they still remain up. It tends to be perceived as a marketing friendly thing, and a lot of people took dislike that/took it as the canary in the coalmine.

In addition imgur just went through a minor situation where they were going to crack down on nsfw comments. The imgur community reacted very predictably to this, and it led to the first time I've ever seen a company issue a public statement/rapid retreat that includes the word dickbutt, so there is that.

TLDR; The internet tends to react very quickly and violently to any perceived censorship, whether there is any or not, mostly for good reasons.Imgur is suffering partially through their perceived actions, and partially due to guilt by association.
